description:
FILED s431 (Opus 5) by the P1 flip census: the four remaining t/op/lexsub.t drops (448, 751, 836, 851) are all this family, and it has no OPEN owner (#361 and #376 are completed).

PROBES (perl 5.40.3):

    { my sub x { 7 } print x, "\n"; }        perl 7      PCL 7        (right)
    { my sub x { 7 } x; print "called\n"; }  perl called PCL DROP  (and the print is inside the dropped text)
    { my sub y { 8 } print y, "\n"; }        perl 8      PCL 0        <- SILENT WRONG

PPI lexes a Word `x` as the repetition operator and `y` as the transliteration operator (docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md section 19 covers `x` after a LIST OPERATOR only).  s430/B3.3 made a lexical sub named after a STATEMENT MODIFIER (`if`) position-aware in the renamer; a QUOTE-LIKE operator name is the sibling case and was not covered -- `y` additionally swallows source as a transliteration, which is how `print y, "\n"` becomes 0.

CENSUS ROWS OWNED: t/op/lexsub.t 448 (`x` as a whole statement), 751 (`x();`), 836 (`x`), 851 (`is y, 43, ...` -- PPI's `y` swallows the following two blocks, including `my sub UTF8NAME`).  op/lexsub.t passes 9 of 156 rows today; #381 (indirect object) is the other thing that file sits behind.

BAR: the three probes + the inverse (a REAL `x`/`y` operator next to a lexical sub of that name: `my sub x {7}; print "a" x 3;`), the s430 position classifier as the model, gate-SET scan over both populations, corpus-diff, guards in Pl/t/lexical-sub-0*.t.
subject: A lexical sub named `y` is SILENT WRONG (`{ my sub y {8} print y, "\n" }` prints 0, perl 8) and a bare `x;` statement-position call DROPS -- the two quote-like-operator names #361/#376 did not cover
